subject: Community Control Over Public Surveillance Ordinance
overview: Hosts discuss the history and implementation of the Community Control Over Public Surveillance (CCOPS) ordinance with a grassroots advocate and a City Councilor. The conversation explores how the ordinance ensures transparency for municipal surveillance technology and protects the civil liberties of Medford residents.

items.title: Introduction and Local Favorites
items.summary: The hosts introduced guests Jean Zotter and Kit Collins, who shared their favorite local dining spots as an icebreaker.

items.title: Defining CCOPS and Surveillance Risks
items.summary: Jean Zotter defined CCOPS as a legal mechanism requiring public input and City Council approval for surveillance technology to ensure municipal accountability and transparency.

items.title: Legislative Motivation and Financial Oversight
items.summary: Councilor Kit Collins discussed the importance of the ordinance for managing the high costs of surveillance technology and preventing the exacerbation of over-policing in marginalized communities.

items.title: Medford People Power and Community Advocacy
items.summary: Zotter detailed the history of Medford People Power, noting their origins in 2017 and their previous success passing a non-cooperation policy regarding ICE.

items.title: Ordinance Procedures and Reporting Requirements
items.summary: The guests explained the administrative process where city agencies must present technology use policies and file annual reports matching actual usage to stated purposes.

items.title: Negotiated Exemptions and Policy Limitations
items.summary: Participants discussed compromises in the final ordinance, including the exclusion of bulk data purchasing and a five-year exemption for body-worn cameras.

items.title: Future Technological Trends and State Legislation
items.summary: The panel reviewed emerging threats from app-based location data and advocacy for the state-level Location Shield Act to protect privacy beyond municipal borders.
